answer.evidence: All 16 conv1 filters exhibit classic, smooth Gabor-like edge detectors (vertical, horizontal, diagonal) and standard color-opponent channels (red-cyan, blue-yellow, green-magenta), with zero high-frequency, checkerboard, or color-noise anomalies. Weights and biases across all layers (conv1 through fc) are remarkably well-regularized with standard distributions (maximum FC weight magnitude is ~0.95). Conv3 features and FC weights exhibit balanced, standard semantic specialization across all CIFAR-10 classes without any dominant backdoor channel. If forced to identify a target class, class 9 (truck) exhibits the highest positive FC weights (e.g., ch 3 at +99, ch 32 at +72), but these appear to be normal class-specific features. Trigger pattern and corner cannot be reliably inferred as the network shows strong evidence of being trained on clean data.
